I’ve just launched the third training run (run_fast3_2b) in the background with the OOM‑handling fix applied to the STM backward pass. The command is running asynchronously, and I set up a background watcher that will poll the log file until it sees either “instruct results:” or a traceback, then extract the final metrics. 

Now I need to ensure that I will come back to process the results once the run finishes. The previous pattern was to schedule a wake‑up an hour later as a fallback, in case the background task hangs or the notification isn’t delivered promptly. The earlier wake‑up was scheduled for the first run (run_fast2_2b) with a similar prompt describing what to do when the log is ready: add rows to scores.md, journal the results, compare throughput, and report to the user.

Given that the new run (run_fast3_2b) includes the backward‑OOM fix, I must adjust the prompt to reflect the updated commit identifiers (the same 28cf7be and 58fb61f plus the latest commit that introduced the fix) and note that the live training throughput should be around 1.19 Mtok/s (the same improvement we saw earlier). The prompt should also ask to capture any OOM shrink prints from the STM/SFT phases, because those are now part of the expected output.

I should schedule the wake‑up for roughly an hour from now (3600 seconds) to give the run ample time (it may take ~30 minutes for training plus some extra for the STM phase). The reason field should mention that this is the “2B run relaunched with backward‑OOM fix; fallback check in 1h”. The prompt field must contain the exact instructions for what to do when the wake‑up fires: check /tmp/run_fast3_2b.log, when the results are printed, add rows to scores.md for the throughput‑restructure run (commits 28cf7be/58fb61f/latest), journal the verbatim results including any OOM shrink prints, commit, and then report to the user with the throughput ladder (dense 2.4 Mtok/s, old sparse 0.85, new 1.19+ Mtok/s) and scores versus the baselines 60.40 and 60.41, plus pros/cons. If the log still isn’t finished, reschedule another wake‑up.

All of this matches the pattern used previously and ensures I’ll handle the results correctly. Therefore I will issue a ScheduleWakeup tool call with these parameters.
